decision: accept (report-only; Rev 2.1 deviation disclosed; nothing on the dashboard)
allowed_wording: Cloud-reported ODO (interpolated) is available at both ends for 584 of 717 logged drives. For identity-class drives of 2 km or more (418 drives, 130 days) the cloud-reported distance exceeds the logged/app-calculated distance by a median 0.110 km [0.098, 0.130]. The aggregate relative difference is +1.20 % [1.04, 1.40] (E_int, day-clustered bootstrap): not consistent within +-1 %, consistent within +-3 %; small difference, cloud larger. Same sign under E_br (+1.23 %), E_near and the +16 s shift (+1.15 %, different sample). Blind audit reproduced +1.17 % [1.03, 1.39] on 420/130. Both counters rest on the same wheel-speed scale, so this checks logging completeness, not distance accuracy. Never use accurate/accuracy, error, correction, true/reference/measured distance.
conditions: state the Rev 2.1 rule change and that the smoke run (+1.13 %) was seen before it; verdict unchanged under both rules
disclose 17 (tool) vs 7 (auditor) jump-excluded drives and 418 vs 420 n; both give the same verdict
disclose availability selection by month and by length; selection effect not excluded
disclose 17 level excursions (max 101.35 km) and 17 negative steps in the cloud stream
anchor is n=1, one-sided plausibility (-0.41 km), not a known answer

cause wording: consistent with logger edge losses (a hypothesis); per-sample speed quantisation in the app integral is an untested alternative; the positive E_int sign argues against a parked-edge interpolation artefact
risks: month and length selection may shift the aggregate
E_int and E_br do not form the expected bracket (both positive), so the edge model of 9.1 is not confirmed
x1_follow_up: may be proposed only as a separate spec addendum with its own Director ruling: wording difference, no absolute cloud ODO (M749), carry the selection and same-scale caveats; resolve or document the jump-rule difference first; not part of M752
